data.summary:
Seven new test files, all additive, mapped to the criteria:

1. `domain/StaleProblemTest` — criteria 1 & 2. `ProblemCode.values()` must be exactly the five existing constants in order with `STALE` appended last. `Problem.stale(3, "R-7", 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z, PT30D)` must carry inputIndex 3, requestId "R-7", code STALE, field "requestedAt", null relatedRequestId/escalatedFrom/escalatedTo, and the exact message `R-7 is stale: requestedAt 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z is more than 30 days old`; a separate test pins the day count to `maxAge` (7d → "7 days old") and another asserts the message never contains the input index.

2. `processing/StalenessValidationTest` — criteria 3–7 (validator side), fixed clock `2026-10-20T08:00:00Z`/30 days via `new WorkRequestValidator(Clock, Duration)`. Covers: stale R-1 dropped while R-2 stays in `StageResult.requests`; exactly one STALE problem for R-1 at index 0 with field "requestedAt"; the boundary trio — exactly 30 days accepted, one second older flagged (and it alone), future date accepted; `clock.instant()` read exactly once per `validate` call (Mockito-verified, so every request shares one "now"); precedence — a null element yields only NULL_REQUEST, a 90-day-old request missing equipmentId yields only that MISSING_FIELD, and a 90-day-old request whose requestedAt is reported in `invalidFieldsByIndex` yields only INVALID_VALUE, plus every STALE problem has a non-null requestId; trace is stage "validate", in 3, out 1, notes exactly `["R-3 rejected: missing description", "R-7 rejected: stale"]`; backwards compatibility — `new WorkRequestValidator()` accepts years-old requests with no problems, and the same through `new WorkRequestProcessor(new WorkRequestValidator(), new DuplicateResolver(new DescriptionNormalizer()), new WorkRequestSorter())`; constructor guards NPE "clock", NPE "maxAge", and IllegalArgumentException for 23h.

3. `processing/StalenessOrderIndependenceTest` — criterion 9. Fixed-clock validator plus the real resolver/sorter over a batch with recent MEDIUM R-1 and 90-day-old CRITICAL R-2 (same equipmentId and description), a duplicate pair, a request missing equipmentId, another stale request and a null element. 100 seeded shuffles must give the identical queue (sequence), the identical problem set (normalised without the shifting input index) and the identical trace. Separate tests: R-2 produces only STALE and never DUPLICATE; R-1 stays queued at MEDIUM; no problem carries an escalation; trace is validate/deduplicate/prioritize with validate.out == deduplicate.in; validate-stage problems precede deduplicate-stage problems; validate-stage problems are ordered by input index with stale and field problems interleaved (STALE R-2, MISSING_FIELD R-5, STALE R-6, NULL_REQUEST).

4. `config/StalenessPropertiesTest` — criterion 7 (properties). Binds to 30 days with no property, 7 days with `app.staleness.max-age=7d`, and fails startup for `0d` and `23h` with `IllegalArgumentException` whose stack trace contains "app.staleness.max-age must be at least 1 day".

5. `config/ClockBeanTest` — criterion 8 (bean shape). `ProcessingConfig` must expose exactly one `java.time.Clock` bean named "clock" equal to `Clock.systemUTC()`, and a single `WorkRequestValidator` bean.

6. `config/StaleRequestWiringTest` — criterion 8 (behaviour). Full context with the clock bean replaced by `Clock.fixed(2026-10-20T08:00:00Z, UTC)`: the application default maxAge is 30 days (from application.yml), the wired pipeline reports a STALE problem with field "requestedAt" for the 90-day-old request and keeps it out of the queue. I verify this through the wired `WorkRequestProcessor` rather than a guessed HTTP path, since the controller route is not named in the criteria and DTO mapping is already pinned by the existing controller tests.

7. `config/ConfiguredStalenessMaxAgeWiringTest` — criterion 8 (threshold comes from config, not a constant): with `app.staleness.max-age=7d` and the same fixed clock, an 8-day-old request is STALE and a 6-day-old one is accepted.

8. `api/StaleProblemMetricsTest` — criterion 9 (metrics): `BatchObserver` registers `workrequests.rejected{code=STALE}` up front and increments it once per stale problem (two stale problems → 2.0).

Only new files under `backend/src/test/java/`; nothing existing is touched, and the staleness-aware behaviour is only exercised through explicitly constructed fixed clocks and explicit timestamps.
